g.aria-label: Designs should keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate, timely feedback.

path.aria-label: Interactive mall maps have to show people where they currently are, to help them understand where to go next.

g.aria-label: The design should speak the users' language. Use words, phrases, and concepts familiar to the user, rather than internal jargon.

path.aria-label: Match between System and the Real World
Users can quickly understand which stovetop control maps to each heating element.

g.aria-label: Good error messages are important, but the best designs carefully prevent problems from occurring in the frst place.

path.aria-label: Guard rails on curvy mountain roads prevent drivers from falling of clifs.

g.aria-label: Users ofen perform actions by mistake. They need a clearly marked "emergency exit" to leave the unwanted action.

path.aria-label: Just like physical spaces, digital spaces need quick “emergency” exits too.

g.aria-label: Minimize the user's memory load by making elements, actions, and options visible. Avoid making users remember information.

path.aria-label: People are likely to correctly answer “Is Lisbon the capital of Portugal?”.

g.aria-label: Users should not have to wonder whether diferent words, situations, or actions mean the same thing. Follow platform conventions.

path.aria-label: Check-in counters are usually located at the front of hotels, which meets expectations.

g.aria-label: Interfaces should not contain information which is irrelevant. Every extra unit of information in an interface competes with the relevant units of information.

path.aria-label: A minimalist three-legged stool is still a place to sit.
Error messages should be expressed in plain language (no error codes), precisely indicate the problem, and constructively suggest a solution.
Wrong-way signs on the road remind drivers that they are heading in the wrong direction.

g.aria-label: Shortcuts — hidden from novice users — may speed up the interaction for the expert user.

path.aria-label: Regular routes are listed on maps, but locals with more knowledge of the area can take shortcuts.

g.aria-label: It’s best if the design doesn’t need any additional explanation. However, it may be necessary to provide documentation to help users complete their tasks.

path.aria-label: Information kiosks at airports are easily recognizable and solve customers' problems in context and immediately.
